document.title: Present Pakistani Initiatives in Afghanistan
document.authors: United Nations Special Mission to Afghanistan (Islamabad)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Taliban File Update
document.note: [Unclassified] Norbert Holl reports on his meeting with Pakistan Foreign Ministry official Iftikhar Murshed, who describes Nawaz Sharif's call and meeting with Taliban official Mullah Rabbani, in which Sharif bluntly demanded a goodwill gesture toward other factions and a meeting with President Rabbani. Murshed also comments on the G8 meeting on Afghanistan, the Afghan UN seat and oil embargoes, calling the meeting a non-event.

persons.name: Norbert H. Holl
persons.role: Head of the UN Special Mission to Afghanistan (UNSMA), Islamabad; author of the cable

mentions.quote: YESTERDAY, 29 OCTOBER, I MET AS MURSHID TO DISCUSS CURRENT PAKISTANI INITIATIVES WITH RESPECT TO AFGHANISTAN
THE FOLLOWING DAY, 16 OCTOBER, I TRAVELED TO KABUL MYSELF AND TALKED TO THE NEW FOREIGN MINISTER MOHAMMED HASSAN

persons.name: Lakhdar Brahimi
persons.role: UN Special Envoy for Afghanistan; intended recipient of the passed message

mentions.quote: REF. FAX AMBASSADOR BRAHIMI, DATED 29 OCTOBER 1997
I WOULD APPRECIATE IF YOU COULD PASS THIS MESSAGE SPEEDILY TO AMBASSADOR B[RAHI]MI

persons.name: Murshid
persons.role: Pakistani Foreign Office official (apparently Additional Secretary, 'AS') handling Afghanistan; Holl's interlocutor

mentions.quote: FS SHAMSHAD AND MURSHID WERE ALSO PRESENT
MURSHID SEEMED TO SHARE MY SKEPTICISM THAT LEADERS LIKE RABBANI AND MASOUD COULD AGREE TO TRAVEL TO ISLAMABAD
NAWAZ SHARIF HAD TELEPHONED MULLAH RABBANI. HE EXPRESSED HIS GROWING IMPATIENCE WITH THE LACK OF PROGRESS
THE PM BLUNTLY DEMANDED THAT THE TALIBAN SHOULD MAKE A GESTURE OF GOODWILL

persons.name: Mullah Rabbani
persons.role: Head of the Taliban government in Kabul (Taliban Prime Minister)

mentions.quote: RABBANI ACCEPTED THE INVITATION. IN THE EVENING OF THE SAME DAY, HE MET NAWAZ SHARIF FOR A LENGTHY DISCUSSION
HE FINALLY AGREED TO MEET WITH ALL THE FOUR LEADERS AT THE SAME TIME
THE MORE POSITIVE STATEMENT OF THE TALIBAN PRIME MINISTER

persons.name: Burhanuddin Rabbani
persons.role: Ousted Afghan president recognized by UN; Northern Alliance leader, based in Faizabad

mentions.quote: MULLAH RABBANI REFUSED TO DO THIS, CLAIMING THAT PROFESSOR RABBANI WAS A MAN WITHOUT POLITICAL RELEVANCE
RUSTAM DECIDED TO FLY TO FAIZABAD, WHERE HE MET PROFESSOR RABBANI

persons.name: Rustam Shah Mohmand
persons.role: Chief Secretary (NWFP) sent by Pakistani PM as envoy to northern Afghan leaders

mentions.quote: RUSTAM'S TRIP TO THE NORTH WAS A FOLLOW UP TO THE PRIME MINISTER'S INITIATIVE
HE TOLD ME THAT RUSTAM HAD MADE NO PROGRESS

persons.name: Ahmad Shah Massoud
persons.role: Northern Alliance military leader, one of the 'Big 4'

mentions.quote: ALL THE FOUR LEADERS AT THE SAME TIME, NAMELY: PROFESSOR RABBANI, MASOUD, DOSTUM, KHALILI

persons.name: Abdul Rashid Dostum
persons.role: Uzbek northern leader based in Mazar; one of the 'Big 4'

mentions.quote: FIRST RUSTAM WANTED TO FLY TO MAZAR, IN ORDER TO TALK TO DOSTUM

persons.name: Karim Khalili
persons.role: Hazara (Hizb-i Wahdat) leader, one of the 'Big 4'

mentions.quote: PROFESSOR RABBANI, MASOUD, DOSTUM, KHALILI. THE MEETING SHOULD TAKE PLACE IN ISLAMABAD
THE NEW FOREIGN MINISTER MOHAMMED HASSAN, WHO REJECTED MORE ADAMANTLY THAN EVER ANY NEGOTIATIONS WITH THE NORTHERN ALLIANCE
FS SHAMSHAD AND MURSHID WERE ALSO PRESENT

persons.name: Karl Inderfurth
persons.role: US Assistant Secretary of State; represented US at 16 Oct meeting

mentions.quote: ALL COUNTRIES (WITH THE EXCEPTION OF THE US - ASS. INDERFURTH) HAD BEEN REPRESENTED ONLY BY THEIR PERMANENT UN REPRESENTATIVES

persons.name: Thomas Pickering
persons.role: US Under Secretary of State, visited Pakistan and held talks with GOP

mentions.quote: PICKERING DID NOT GIVE IN TO THESE PAKISTANI REQUESTS

events.description: Nawaz Sharif phoned Mullah Rabbani in the morning, invited him to Islamabad; that evening they met and dined, with FS Shamshad and Murshid present; Rabbani agreed to meet the four Northern leaders.
Holl travelled to Kabul and met Taliban FM Mohammed Hassan, who rejected negotiations with the Northern Alliance.
First round of the 'G8' (6+2) meeting on Afghanistan, judged a non-event; Pakistan isolated on proposals to vacate Afghan seat and impose arms embargo.
Pakistani Foreign Office published statement on Rabbani's visit after Nawaz Sharif criticized the omission.
Rustam Shah denied flight clearance to Mazar, instead flew to Faizabad and met Professor Rabbani; no progress on 'Big 4' meeting.
US Under Secretary Pickering held talks with GOP (PM, FM, FS, AS) in Islamabad, refusing to back Afghan-seat vacancy and arms embargo, and failing to win POL and wheat embargo.
Holl met Murshid, and separately US Ambassador Simons, in Islamabad.
Pakistan due to sign new contract to supply 600,000 tons of wheat to Afghanistan for 12 months.
Nawaz Sharif phoned Mullah Rabbani, who flew to Islamabad and met Sharif for discussion and dinner; he agreed to meet the four Northern leaders in Islamabad.
First round of the Six plus Two (G8 in cable) meeting, described as a non-event; Pakistan isolated on vacant seat and arms embargo proposals.
Holl traveled to Kabul and met Taliban foreign minister Mohammed Hassan, who rejected talks with the Northern Alliance.
Pakistani Foreign Office published statement on Mullah Rabbani's visit after Sharif's instruction.
Rustam Shah Mohmand denied flight clearance to Mazar, flew instead to Faizabad and met Professor Rabbani, who reacted evasively.
Holl met Murshid on Pakistani initiatives, and met US Ambassador Simons.
Pakistan to sign new contract for 600,000 tons of wheat for 12 months for Afghanistan.
Pickering held talks with Pakistani government; Pakistan requested US support to declare Afghan seat vacant and arms embargo; Pickering refused and failed to win POL/wheat embargo.

sources_cited: UNSMA fax from Ambassador Brahimi dated 29 October 1997 (reference)
Dr. Kamal's report on the 16 October G8 meeting (OCR garbled)
key_claims: Pakistan's PM pressed the Taliban's Mullah Rabbani to meet the four Northern Alliance leaders in Islamabad, which he accepted on 15 Oct 1997 without raising the POW/VIP precondition.
Taliban foreign minister Hassan rejected any negotiation with the Northern Alliance the day after, showing a gap between the Taliban PM's stance and Kabul's position.
Pakistan's attempts to declare the Afghan UN seat vacant and impose an arms embargo were isolated at the 16 Oct meeting; it refused an oil embargo.
Saudi Arabia funded POL supplies to Afghanistan, previously going to the Rabbani regime and now to the Taliban, which Pakistan would not impede.
Pakistan signed a 12-month, 600,000-ton wheat supply contract with Afghanistan on 30 Oct 1997 despite US pressure.
Rustam Shah's mission to Faizabad made no progress; Professor Rabbani was evasive and Dostum could not be reached.
US officials judged Pakistan to be buying time but increasingly facing international pressure from traditional friends.
